lead_headline: Restaurant tracker logs 6 new leads as FiNO debuts at All Inn Hotel and Super Mega Bien closes after 8-year RiNo run

restaurant.blurb: 6 new leads today bring active roster to 53 total (25 openings, 28 closures)—opening side gains FiNO's Mediterranean debut at renovated All Inn Hotel (City Park, soft open March 18) while closure wave adds Super Mega Bien's shutdown (Five Points, 8-year RiNo staple citing financial pressures, closed March 14) and Menya on Havana's four-month flameout (Kennedy, Seoul Hospitality Group casualty, shuttered Jan 1). Closures reclaim lead by 3 after Tuesday's brief parity—28 vs 25 marks widest gap since March 10. Geographic spread: Union Station churn persists (Mopoke, FiNO parent All Inn), Kennedy sees back-to-back failures (Menya, prior Tandoori Halal), Capitol Hill hemorrhage continues post-tax seizures.

foreclosure.blurb: 30 filings this week hold March floor for third consecutive period—9% decline from prior week's 33 extends five-week descent but stabilizes at 30-threshold baseline. 105 auctions scheduled next seven days (up 4 from yesterday's 101), $11.2M total exposure static. Arapahoe's $2.24M South Columbine Circle remains sole seven-figure property this cycle—Weld's $618K Falcon Drive ranks distant second. County landscape: El Paso leads at 475 active cases, Weld 407, Arapahoe 415—exurban concentration locked. Weekly filing rate plateaus: three straight 30-33 readings suggest March discovered seasonal floor, tracking 40% below January's 50-filing peak.

reputation.blurb: 6 mentions yesterday pull seven-day total to 39 citations across 11 sources—down 19% from prior week's 48, erasing Tuesday's 10-mention surge and resuming two-week decline trajectory. Denver Post commands 38% share (15 of 39), social platforms (Facebook/Instagram/X) aggregate 13 pickups, Hoodline adds 5. Notable Wednesday detections: Cathedral High campus receiver story, LoDo office sale, shopping center facelift coverage. Yesterday's 6-mention drop (from Tuesday's 10) signals volatility—single-day swings mask underlying 39-48 band compression. Pattern: Post-driven cycle dependency exposes narrow sourcing risk as Google News RSS captures 97% discovery (38 of 39). Monthly pace: 107 total suggests 142-month trajectory if sustained.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (4 new, 3 canceled) lifts MTD to +28 (+1.6/day), 90-day cumulative at +91. Wednesday churn (3 cancellations) tests recent retention discipline but acquisition pace holds at 4 new—matching March 16-18 floor. Seven-day window: +16 net (20 new, 4 canceled) outpaces prior week's +12 by 33%, driven by cancellation compression (4 vs 15). March's 1.6/day rate tracks 23% above YTD's 1.3/day benchmark—strongest monthly pace since tracker launch. Recent pattern: post-March 5 volatility (-4 net) absorbed, sub-acquisition stabilizes at 3-5 daily range with cancellations contained below 2/day. Momentum intact despite Wednesday's 3-cancel wobble.
